title: Copperlane healthcare outbound notes
content:
Quick scratchpad for Copperlane (regional health tech provider) — research + outbound + objections. Notes to self, not polished.

Account snapshot:
- Name: Copperlane Health Systems (regional chain; ~8 hospitals + ambulatory clinics)
- HQ: Midwest
- Estimated scale: 200k annual patient visits, EMR = MedStream v6 (custom integrations team)
- Likely buyer: Dir of Clinical Ops (Elena Martinez) + Head of IT (Samir Rao) + Compliance (privacy officer)
- Recent signals: press release (2025-09) about telehealth expansion; job posting for 'AI/Clinical Informatics' (hiring).

Hypothesized pain points:
- High triage load on nursing lines -> long wait times
- Physician documentation time (notes) causing burnout
- Internal triage chatbot is brittle, low NLU accuracy for regional dialects/phrases
- Risk/Compliance: need PHI-safe models (on-prem/VPC) and audit trails

Why Redwood could matter (value prop hypotheses):
- Reduce average triage call handle time via streaming LLM assistant + KV cache of patient context -> cost savings for contact center
- Document drafts and summarization workflows to shave provider notes time (15-25% reduction target)
- Private deployment option satisfies PHI (Private / Dedicated) + KMS integration for keys/audit
- Observability: token-level cost and latency dashboards to justify ROI to finance

Priority outreach goals (first 60 days):
1) Intro to Elena Martinez + Samir Rao (confirm who owns vendor decisions)
2) Land a 30-minute discovery call to validate triage + documentation pain (not a product demo)
3) Propose small pilot: 4-week triage assistant pilot on 1 clinic intake line (clear OKRs)

Subject line ideas (A/B test):
- "Pilot idea: reduce triage hold times at Copperlane"
- "Quick intro — helping regional health systems cut note time by ~20%"
- "Private LLM pilot for Copperlane — PHI-compliant, low-risk"

Cold email - short opener (version A):
Hi Elena —
Saw Copperlane's telehealth expansion announcement and your AI/Clinical Informatics hire. We help regional health systems reduce triage hold times and save provider documentation time using private, audit-ready LLM deployments.
Would 20 minutes next week be useful to explore a low-risk 4-week pilot scoped to an intake line? No IP required; we handle PHI controls and provide clear ROI metrics.
— Aisha

Follow-up (2 days later):
Quick note — if now isn't the right time, who on your team runs triage ops or clinical documentation improvement? Happy to connect with them.

Call script / discovery playbook (30 min):
- 0–3 min: intro, reason for reach, one-sentence credential (e.g., "we run private inference for hospitals; we helped X reduce triage AHT by 18% in a 6-week pilot")
- 3–12 min: discovery: top metrics and owners
  - Who measures triage hold times right now?
  - Typical AHT / abandonment rate? Target reductions?
  - Where does documentation time get captured? EHR metrics?
  - Who would own an internal pilot (nursing ops, clinical informatics, IT)?
- 12–22 min: workflows + constraints
  - Walk me through a triage call / intake -> what systems are touched? (phone platform, EHR, care management)
  - Any live IVR / bot today? If so, where does it break?
  - Compliance: PHI handling requirements; do you need on-prem or VPC? SOC2 / HIPAA posture?
- 22–28 min: pilot framing (scope, success metrics, timeline, data needs)
- 28–30 min: next steps, internal stakeholders, propose a pilot plan email

Objection handling cheatsheet (short, quick rebuttals):
- "We can't use external models with PHI" -> Redwood Private or Dedicated + KMS/HSM option, full audit logs; we can run inside their VPC or on-prem package.
- "Too risky / long procurement" -> Offer a technical pilot under MSLA or short PoC MOU; we support a sandbox with synthetic data to prove flow first.
- "We already have an internal chatbot" -> Ask about measured impact; offer augmentation (KV cache + role-conditioned responses) rather than full rip-and-replace. Small trial on a single queue so ops can compare.
- "Provider adoption concerns" -> Start with provider-facing drafts (notes suggestions) rather than autonomous actions; always present "suggested" output vs autopopulate. Training + feedback loop in the pilot.
- "Cost / ROI unclear" -> Anchor: typical triage AHT reduction -> X calls/day * time saved * staff hourly = monthly savings. We'll run a 4-week baseline to measure.

Pricing anchor (internal note):
- For pilot: propose $15k–25k fixed pilot fee (deployment + 4 weeks support + monitoring + evaluation). Rationale: dedicated infra + customization + compliance. Use slide with TCO comparison vs labor cost.

Pilot success metrics (suggested):
- Baseline and post-pilot AHT for triage queue (target 10–20% reduction)
- Provider notes time saved per shift (target 15% reduction)
- False positive/incorrect advice rate < X% (set realistic threshold with clinical governance)
- Adoption: % of providers using suggestions > 50% within pilot scope

Data / tech checklist to ask for during discovery:
- Phone platform + APIs (Twilio? Avaya?), call recording access?
- EHR access pattern: read-only patient context, de-identified test data for sandbox
- Legal/Privacy: contact for DPA / BAAs; list of required compliance reports
- Network: possibility for VPC peering or on-prem appliance install window

Notes to self / open questions:
- Who at Redwood owns the on-prem package handoff? Need SRE/infra contact for pre-sales (ask Marc).
- Confirm definitive pilot pricing ranges with finance (Riley to confirm).
- Do we have prior health-care case study we can show for triage or notes? If not, create a one-pager with synthetic ROI.
- For Elena — check LinkedIn mutual connections (possible warm intro).

Draft outreach Slack DM (internal):
@Marc Liu can you share the on-prem install runbook? Elena's team will ask about deployment windows and we should have a short answer. Also need an example BAAs we use for hospitals.

Next steps (action items):
- [ ] Send initial email to Elena + Samir with A/B subject lines (pick one, send Tue morning)
- [ ] Confirm pilot pricing band with Riley by EOD Friday
- [ ] Prep a 1-page pilot scoping doc (template) to attach to outreach (target: 1–pager, < 1 page)
- [ ] Pull any healthcare case studies / anonymized metrics to include (if none, create synthetic ROI slide)

Quick voice memo summary (for follow-up):
- Keep ask focused: 20-min discovery -> 4-week low-risk pilot. Emphasize PHI controls and clear ROI measurement.

---
Tiny iteration ideas (future):
- Create a short checklist 'PHI-ready pilot — 5 things legal will ask' to include in initial email so compliance feels pre-empted.
- Run an outbound A/B test: clinical-ops focused copy vs IT/compliance-focused copy and measure reply rate.

End of scratchpad.
